summary: @onereach/regular-expressions preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727KB payload
details: The package declares itself as a Vue components library for regular expressions but ships a `preinstall` hook `node setup.mjs` that downloads the Bun runtime (bun v1.3.13) from GitHub releases at install time and uses it to execute a sibling file `math_init.js` — a 727,680-byte obfuscator.io-style bundle with shuffled string arrays (`n7gIxM` rotated by `WV8StW`), single-letter/hex-suffixed identifiers, and no readable strings. The bundle is invoked via `execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')])`. The payload bears no relation to the package's advertised regex/Vue-components purpose, its filename (`math_init`) is unrelated to that purpose, and executing it under a freshly downloaded alternate runtime isolates the code from Node-side inspection. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: install-time execution of opaque, obfuscated code that does not correspond to the package's stated function.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
